summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of gold investments in India, with most factual claims being accurate. However, there are some inaccuracies regarding the tax treatment of Sovereign Gold Bonds and the holding period for long-term capital gains on Gold ETFs and Mutual Funds, which could mislead investors.

claims.claim: SGBs offer a fixed interest rate of 2.50% per annum on the initial investment amount, paid semi-annually.
claims.note: The RBI and other financial institutions confirm a fixed interest rate of 2.50% per annum, paid semi-annually on SGBs.

claims.claim: Capital gains arising from redemption of SGBs by an individual are exempt from tax.
claims.note: As per the Finance Act 2026, capital gains on SGBs are exempt from tax only for original subscribers who hold them until maturity (8 years). If SGBs are bought from the secondary market or redeemed prematurely, capital gains tax is applicable.

claims.claim: SGBs have a maturity period of 8 years with an exit option after the 5th year.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the 8-year maturity period for SGBs with an exit option after the 5th year, exercisable on interest payment dates.

claims.claim: Each unit of a Gold ETF typically represents one gram of gold.
claims.note: AMFI and other financial institutions state that each unit of a Gold ETF typically represents one gram of 99.5% pure physical gold.

claims.claim: Gold ETFs are open-ended mutual funds that invest in 99.5% pure physical gold.
claims.note: Gold ETFs are indeed open-ended mutual funds that invest in 99.5% pure physical gold.

claims.claim: For Gold ETFs and Gold Mutual Funds, capital gains are taxed based on the holding period. Short-term capital gains (held for 36 months or less) are added to your income and taxed as per your slab, while long-term capital gains (held for more than 36 months) are taxed at 20% with indexation benefits.
claims.note: The holding period for LTCG on Gold ETFs is more than 12 months, and for Gold Mutual Funds, it's more than 24 months. The tax rate for LTCG on these is 12.5% without indexation benefits, as per recent changes (effective July 23, 2024, for transfers).

claims.claim: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can invest in various forms of gold in India, including physical gold, Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs), and Gold Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), subject to FEMA regulations.
claims.note: NRIs are generally NOT permitted to make fresh investments in Sovereign Gold Bonds as per FEMA regulations. They can, however, continue to hold SGBs purchased when they were residents or acquire them through inheritance/gifts.
